reasoning_content: catalog.ttl has no `dcat:accessURL` match in that format — there are 46 references to `http://localhost`. So the distribution URLs point to `http://localhost:8000/...`, and the test server is running on port 8000. My server is on 8123. The script should report most of the links as inaccessible (connection refused on port 8000), but that's still a valid run — it processes the catalog and writes out JSONL results. In fact, the integration tests were using port 8000. To do a faithful end-to-end run, I should serve on port 8000 instead. Let me kill the 8123 server and use 8000.

action.command:
kill 14031 2>/dev/null; sleep 1; cd /workspace/tests/data && nohup python3 -m http.server 8000 > /tmp/http_server.log 2>&1 &
echo "server $!"; sleep 2; curl -s -o /dev/null -w "catalog.ttl: %{http_code}\n" http://localhost:8000/catalog.ttl

tool_call.name: terminal
